sections.title: Section I
sections.instructions: Attempt Questions 1 to 10. Allow about 15 minutes for this section.

stem.t: What is the range of the function $y = 3\sin^{-1}\!\left(\dfrac{x}{4}\right) + 9$?

sampleAnswer.t: $\sin^{-1}$ takes every value from $-\dfrac{\pi}{2}$ to $\dfrac{\pi}{2}$, so $3\sin^{-1}\left(\dfrac{x}{4}\right)$ takes every value from $-\dfrac{3\pi}{2}$ to $\dfrac{3\pi}{2}$. Add 9.

classification.content: Inverse trigonometric functions; range

stem.t: Which graph shows the curve with parametric equations $x = \cos 3t$, $y = \sin 4t$ for $0 \le t \le 2\pi$?

sampleAnswer.t: The curve meets the line $x = 1$ where $\cos 3t = 1$, and the line $y = 1$ where $\sin 4t = 1$. Working out the points gives 3 points on $x = 1$ and 4 points on $y = 1$, which matches only graph B.

classification.content: Parametric equations; sketching curves

stem.t: How many subsets of $\{1, 2, 3, \ldots, 11\}$ have exactly 4 elements, no two of which are consecutive integers?

sampleAnswer.t: Write the chosen numbers as $a_1 < a_2 < \cdots < a_{4}$ and let $b_i = a_i - (i - 1)$. The condition $a_{i+1} \ge a_i + 2$ becomes $b_{i+1} > b_i$, and the $b_i$ are any 4 different numbers from $1$ to $8$. So there are $\dbinom{8}{4} = 70$ subsets.

classification.content: Combinations; choosing with gaps

stem.t: The polynomial $x^4 - 864x + c$ has a repeated zero.

sampleAnswer.t: A repeated zero is a zero of the derivative $4x^3 - 864$, whose only real zero is $x = 6$. Then $1296 - 5184 + c = 0$, so $c = 3888$.

classification.content: Multiple zeros of polynomials

stem.t: How many solutions does the equation $\sin 4x = \sin x$ have for $0 \le x \le 2\pi$?

sampleAnswer.t: $\sin A = \sin B$ exactly when $A = B + 2k\pi$ or $A = \pi - B + 2k\pi$. So $x = \dfrac{2k\pi}{3}$, giving 4 values in $[0, 2\pi]$, or $x = \dfrac{(2k + 1)\pi}{5}$, giving 5 values. No value is counted twice. There are 9 solutions.

classification.content: Trigonometric equations; general solutions

stem.t: The random variable $X$ has a binomial distribution with mean $4$ and variance $\dfrac{16}{5}$.
Which of the following gives the parameters of the distribution?

sampleAnswer.t: $np = 4$ and $np(1 - p) = \dfrac{16}{5}$, so $1 - p = \dfrac{\dfrac{16}{5}}{4}$, giving $p = \dfrac{1}{5}$ and $n = 4 \div \dfrac{1}{5} = 20$.

classification.content: Binomial distribution; mean and variance

stem.t: For which value of $t$ is $\underset{\sim}{a} + t\,\underset{\sim}{b}$ perpendicular to $\underset{\sim}{a} - \underset{\sim}{b}$?

sampleAnswer.t: $\left(\underset{\sim}{a} + t\,\underset{\sim}{b}\right)\cdot\left(\underset{\sim}{a} - \underset{\sim}{b}\right) = \underset{\sim}{a}\cdot(\underset{\sim}{a} - \underset{\sim}{b}) + t\,\underset{\sim}{b}\cdot(\underset{\sim}{a} - \underset{\sim}{b}) = 6 - 3 t = 0$, so $t = 2$.

classification.content: Vectors; scalar product and perpendicularity

stem.t: A fish population $P$ satisfies $\dfrac{dP}{dt} = \dfrac{1}{5}\,P\left(1 - \dfrac{P}{800}\right) - h$, where $h \ge 0$ is the constant rate at which fish are caught.
What is the greatest value of $h$ for which there is a population size that stays constant?

sampleAnswer.t: A constant population needs $\dfrac{dP}{dt} = 0$, that is, $h = \dfrac{1}{5}\,P\left(1 - \dfrac{P}{800}\right)$. The right-hand side is a quadratic in $P$ with greatest value at $P = 400$, where it equals $40$. So $h$ can be at most $40$.

classification.content: Logistic models with harvesting; equilibrium solutions

stem.t: Two particles are projected at the same instant from the same point, with the same speed, at angles of $30^\circ$ and $65^\circ$ to the horizontal. While both are in flight, the line joining them makes a constant acute angle with the horizontal.

sampleAnswer.t: The positions differ by $Vt(\cos\beta - \cos\alpha)\underset{\sim}{i} + Vt(\sin\beta - \sin\alpha)\underset{\sim}{j}$ (the $\tfrac12gt^2$ terms cancel). This is a multiple of $-\sin\tfrac{\alpha + \beta}{2}\,\underset{\sim}{i} + \cos\tfrac{\alpha + \beta}{2}\,\underset{\sim}{j}$, which is perpendicular to the direction at angle $\tfrac{\alpha + \beta}{2} = 47.5^\circ$. So the line makes an angle of $90^\circ - 47.5^\circ = 42.5^\circ$ with the horizontal.

classification.content: Projectile motion in vector form; relative position

stem.t: The tangent to the curve $y = e^{6x}$ at the point where $x = 3$ meets the $x$-axis at $P$.

sampleAnswer.t: At $x = 3$, $y = e^{18}$ and $y' = 6e^{18}$, so the tangent meets $y = 0$ where $x = 3 - \dfrac{1}{6} = \dfrac{17}{6}$.

classification.content: Tangents; derivatives of powers and exponentials

sections.title: Section II
sections.instructions: Attempt Questions 11 to 14. Allow about 1 hour and 45 minutes for this section. Show relevant mathematical reasoning and/or calculations.

parts.label: (a)

prompt.t: Find $y$ as a function of $x$, given that $\dfrac{dy}{dx} = \left(1 + y^2\right)\cos x$ and $y(0) = 0$.

sampleAnswer.t: $\displaystyle\int\frac{dy}{1 + y^2} = \int\cos x\,dx$ gives $\tan^{-1}y = \sin x + C$. At $x = 0$, $C = \tan^{-1}0$. Hence $y = \tan(\sin x)$.

classification.content: Separable differential equations

parts.keyChecks: verified by tools/papers/verify/p09.py: RK4 integration of dy/dx=(1+y^2)cos x, y(0)=0 vs tan(sin x) at 8 points in [-3,3], max err < 1e-9

prompt.t: Prove by mathematical induction that $8^{n+1} - 7n - 8$ is divisible by $49$ for all integers $n \ge 1$.

text.t: Verifies the base case and makes substantial progress with the inductive step

sampleAnswer.t: When $n = 1$ the expression is $49$, which is divisible by $49$. Assume that the expression for $n = k$ equals $49M$ for an integer $M$. Then for $n = k + 1$: $8^{k+2} - 7(k + 1) - 8 = 8\left(8^{k+1} - 7k - 8\right) + 49k + 49 = 392M + 49k + 49$, which is divisible by $49$. So the result holds for $n = k + 1$, and hence for all $n \ge 1$ by mathematical induction.

classification.content: Proof by induction; divisibility

prompt.t: Let $f(x) = (x + 3)^2 - 3$ for $x \ge -3$, and let $f^{-1}$ be its inverse function.
Find the coordinates of the points where the graphs of $y = f(x)$ and $y = f^{-1}(x)$ meet.

text.t: Explains why the graphs meet only on $y = x$, or solves $f(x) = x$ correctly

sampleAnswer.t: $f$ is increasing for $x \ge -3$. If $f(a) = b$ and $f^{-1}(a) = b$ then $f(b) = a$; if $a < b$ then $f(a) < f(b)$, that is, $b < a$, which is impossible, and similarly $a > b$ is impossible. So the graphs meet only on the line $y = x$, where $f(x) = x$: $x^2 + 5 x + 6 = 0$, so $(x + 3)(x + 2) = 0$. Both values satisfy $x \ge -3$, so the points are $(-3, -3)$ and $(-2, -2)$.

classification.content: Inverse functions; intersections with the inverse

parts.label: (d)

prompt.t: Find the least value of $3\sin^2 x - 4\sin x\cos x - \cos^2 x$.

text.t: Writes the expression in the form $A + R\cos(2x - \alpha)$, or equivalent merit
Uses double-angle results to rewrite the expression

sampleAnswer.t: Using $\sin^2 x = \tfrac12(1 - \cos 2x)$, $\cos^2 x = \tfrac12(1 + \cos 2x)$ and $\sin x\cos x = \tfrac12\sin 2x$, the expression is $1 -2\cos 2x - 2\sin 2x$. Now $-2\cos 2x - 2\sin 2x = 2 \sqrt{2}\cos(2x - \alpha)$ for a suitable angle $\alpha$, and $\cos(2x - \alpha)$ takes every value from $-1$ to $1$. So the least value is $1 - 2 \sqrt{2}$.

classification.content: Double-angle results; auxiliary angle; extreme values

parts.keyChecks: verified by tools/papers/verify/p09.py: fine-grid then golden-section minimum of 3sin^2x-4sinx cosx-cos^2x over [0,2pi]: -1.828427125

parts.label: (e)

prompt.t: Use the substitution $u = x^2 + 4$ to find the exact value of $\displaystyle\int_{0}^{3}\frac{x^3}{\sqrt{x^2 + 4}}\,dx$.

text.t: Obtains a correct primitive in terms of $u$
Transforms the integral and the limits correctly

sampleAnswer.t: Changing the variable and the limits, the integral becomes
\frac12\int_{4}^{13}\frac{u - 4}{\sqrt{u}}\,du = \left[\frac13u^{\frac32} - 4u^{\frac12}\right]_{4}^{13} = \dfrac{\sqrt{13}}{3} + \dfrac{16}{3}.

classification.content: Integration by substitution

parts.keyChecks: verified by tools/papers/verify/p09.py: mpmath quadrature of the original integral to 30 digits

parts.label: (a)

prompt.t: Use vectors to find the coordinates of the point $P$ on the line $AB$ that is closest to $C$.

sampleAnswer.t: $\overrightarrow{AB} = \underset{\sim}{i} - 2\underset{\sim}{j}$ and $\overrightarrow{AC} = 8\underset{\sim}{i} + 5\underset{\sim}{j}$. The closest point is the foot of the perpendicular from $C$, $\overrightarrow{AP} = \dfrac{\overrightarrow{AC}\cdot\overrightarrow{AB}}{\left|\overrightarrow{AB}\right|^2}\overrightarrow{AB} = \dfrac{-2}{5}\overrightarrow{AB}$. So $P$ is $(- \dfrac{22}{5}, \dfrac{4}{5})$.

classification.content: Vector projections; closest point on a line

parts.keyChecks: verified by tools/papers/verify/p09.py: minimisation of |A+t(B-A)-C|^2 over t (SymPy exact)

parts.label: (b)

prompt.t: The random variable $X$ has a binomial distribution with mean $\dfrac{11}{4}$. It is given that $P(X = 2) = P(X = 3)$.
Find the number of trials $n$.

sampleAnswer.t: Equating $\dbinom{n}{2}p^{2}(1 - p)^{n - 2}$ and $\dbinom{n}{3}p^{3}(1 - p)^{n - 3}$ gives $(n - 2)p = 3(1 - p)$, so $p = \dfrac{3}{n + 1}$. Then $np = \dfrac{3n}{n + 1} = \dfrac{11}{4}$, which gives $n = 11$.

classification.content: Binomial probabilities and mean

parts.keyChecks: verified by tools/papers/verify/p09.py: exact Fractions: for n=3..200 with p=11/(4n), P(X=2)=P(X=3) holds only for n=11

prompt.t: A ball is thrown from a point $O$ at the top of a vertical cliff of height $5$ m above flat ground, with speed $20$ m s$^{-1}$ at an angle $\theta$ above the horizontal, where $0 \le \theta < \dfrac{\pi}{2}$. Take $g = 10$ m s$^{-2}$. Its position relative to $O$ at time $t$ is $20t\cos\theta\,\underset{\sim}{i} + \left(20t\sin\theta - 5t^2\right)\underset{\sim}{j}$. It lands at a horizontal distance $R$ from the foot of the cliff.
Show that $\ -5 = R\tan\theta - \dfrac{1}{80}R^2\left(1 + \tan^2\theta\right)$.

text.t: Finds the time of flight in terms of $R$ and $\theta$

sampleAnswer.t: The ball lands when $20t\cos\theta = R$, that is, $t = \dfrac{R}{20\cos\theta}$, and then its height relative to $O$ is $-5$: $\ -5 = R\tan\theta - \dfrac{5R^2}{400\cos^2\theta} = R\tan\theta - \dfrac{1}{80}R^2\left(1 + \tan^2\theta\right)$.

classification.content: Projectile motion; greatest range from a height; quadratics

parts.label: (ii)

prompt.t: By considering this as a quadratic equation in $\tan\theta$, find the greatest possible value of $R$.

text.t: Uses the condition that the discriminant is non-negative
Writes the equation as a quadratic in $\tan\theta$

sampleAnswer.t: With $T = \tan\theta$: $\ \dfrac{1}{80}R^2T^2 - RT + \dfrac{1}{80}R^2 - 5 = 0$. A real value of $T$ exists exactly when the discriminant is non-negative: $R^2 - 4 \times \dfrac{1}{80}R^2\left(\dfrac{1}{80}R^2 - 5\right) \ge 0$, that is, $1 - 4 \times \dfrac{1}{80}\left(\dfrac{1}{80}R^2 - 5\right) \ge 0$, so $R^2 \le 2000$. The greatest value is $R = 20 \sqrt{5}$ m.

classification.content: Projectile motion; greatest range from a height; quadratics

parts.keyChecks: verified by tools/papers/verify/p09.py: landing range from y(t)=-5 maximised over theta in [0,pi/2) (golden section): 44.72135955

parts.label: (iii)

prompt.t: Find the value of $\tan\theta$ that gives this greatest value.

text.t: Recognises that the quadratic has a repeated root

sampleAnswer.t: For the greatest $R$ the quadratic has a repeated root $T = \dfrac{R}{2 \times \dfrac{1}{80}R^2} = \dfrac{1}{2 \times \dfrac{1}{80} R} = \dfrac{2 \sqrt{5}}{5}$.

classification.content: Projectile motion; greatest range from a height; quadratics

parts.keyChecks: verified by tools/papers/verify/p09.py: tan of the maximising theta from the same golden-section search: 0.894427191

prompt.t: For $k \ge 1$ let $T_k = \tan^{-1}\left(\dfrac{2}{4 + k(k - 1)}\right)$, and let $S_n = T_1 + T_2 + \cdots + T_n$.
Show that $T_k = \tan^{-1}\dfrac{k}{2} - \tan^{-1}\dfrac{(k - 1)}{2}$.

sampleAnswer.t: Let $\alpha = \tan^{-1}(\dfrac{1}{2}k)$ and $\beta = \tan^{-1}(\dfrac{1}{2}(k - 1))$, so $0 \le \beta < \alpha < \dfrac{\pi}{2}$. Then $\tan(\alpha - \beta) = \dfrac{\dfrac{1}{2}k - \dfrac{1}{2}(k - 1)}{1 + \dfrac{1}{4}k(k - 1)} = \dfrac{2}{4 + k(k - 1)}$ (multiplying the numerator and denominator by $4$), and $0 < \alpha - \beta < \dfrac{\pi}{2}$, so $\alpha - \beta = T_k$.

classification.content: Inverse tangent; compound angles; telescoping sums

parts.label: (ii)

prompt.t: Find $S_n$ in terms of $n$.

text.t: Writes the sum using part (i) and notes the cancellation

sampleAnswer.t: By part (i) the sum telescopes: $S_n = \tan^{-1}(\dfrac{1}{2}n) - \tan^{-1}0 = \tan^{-1}(\dfrac{1}{2}n)$.

classification.content: Inverse tangent; compound angles; telescoping sums

parts.keyChecks: verified by tools/papers/verify/p09.py: direct summation of T_k in mpmath at 30 digits for n=1..40

parts.label: (iii)

prompt.t: Find the limit of $S_n$ as $n \to \infty$.

sampleAnswer.t: As $n \to \infty$, $\dfrac{1}{2}n \to \infty$, so $S_n \to \dfrac{\pi}{2}$.

classification.content: Inverse tangent; compound angles; telescoping sums

parts.keyChecks: verified by tools/papers/verify/p09.py: mpmath nsum (Richardson) of the series T_k, k>=1, to 30 digits

parts.label: (iv)

prompt.t: Find the smallest $n$ for which $S_n > \dfrac{\pi}{2} - \dfrac{1}{100}$.

text.t: Writes the condition in terms of $\tan$ or $\cot$

sampleAnswer.t: $\tan^{-1}(\dfrac{1}{2}n) > \dfrac{\pi}{2} - \dfrac{1}{100}$ exactly when $\dfrac{1}{2}n > \tan\left(\dfrac{\pi}{2} - \dfrac{1}{100}\right) = \dfrac{1}{\tan \dfrac{1}{100}} \approx 99.997$, since $\tan$ is increasing on $\left(0, \dfrac{\pi}{2}\right)$. So $n > 199.993$, and the smallest $n$ is $200$.

classification.content: Inverse tangent; compound angles; telescoping sums

parts.keyChecks: verified by tools/papers/verify/p09.py: direct partial sums at 40 digits: first n with S_n > pi/2-1/100

prompt.t: A sequence is defined by its first term $a_1$ and the rule $a_{n+1} = 2a_n^2 - 1$ for $n \ge 1$.
Suppose that $a_1 = \cos\theta$. Find $a_2$, $a_3$ and $a_4$ in the form $\cos(\ldots)$, and write down a formula for $a_n$ in terms of $n$ and $\theta$.

text.t: Provides the correct formula with justification

sampleAnswer.t: $a_2 = 2\cos^2\theta - 1 = \cos 2\theta$, so $a_3 = 2\cos^2 2\theta - 1 = \cos 4\theta$ and $a_4 = 2\cos^2 4\theta - 1 = \cos 8\theta$. Each term doubles the angle, so $a_n = \cos\left(2^{n-1}\theta\right)$.

classification.content: Double-angle results; polynomial equations; recurrences

parts.label: (ii)

prompt.t: Suppose that $a_1 = \cos\dfrac{\pi}{64}$. Find the smallest $n$ for which $a_n = 1$.

text.t: Provides the correct value with justification

sampleAnswer.t: By part (i) with $\theta = \dfrac{\pi}{64}$, $a_n = \cos\dfrac{2^{n-1}\pi}{64} = 1$ exactly when $\dfrac{2^{n-1}}{64}$ is an even integer, that is, $2^{n-1} \ge 128$. The smallest $n$ is $8$.

classification.content: Double-angle results; polynomial equations; recurrences

parts.keyChecks: verified by tools/papers/verify/p09.py: iterating a_{n+1}=2a_n^2-1 from cos(pi/64) at 120 digits: first n with a_n=1 (to 1e-100)

parts.label: (iii)

prompt.t: Find all values of $a_1$ for which $a_3 = a_1$.

text.t: Provides all the values with justification
Writes the equation as a polynomial equation in $a_1$ and factorises it, or equivalent merit

sampleAnswer.t: Let $a = a_1$. Then $a_2 = 2a^2 - 1$ and $a_3 = 2\left(2a^2 - 1\right)^2 - 1 = 8a^4 - 8a^2 + 1$. So $a_3 = a$ when $8a^4 - 8a^2 - a + 1 = 0$. Since $a = 1$ is a zero, this factorises as
Hence $a_1 = 1$, $\ a_1 = -\dfrac12$, or $a_1 = \dfrac{-1 \pm \sqrt5}{4}$.

classification.content: Double-angle results; polynomial equations; recurrences

parts.keyChecks: verified by tools/papers/verify/p09.py: real roots of a_3(a)-a=0 with a_3 from two applications of the recurrence (SymPy exact)

prompt.t: A small plane has 12 seats. Each person who buys a ticket turns up for the flight with probability $\dfrac{47}{50}$, independently of the others. Each ticket costs $250, and the airline pays $$C$ in compensation to each passenger who turns up but cannot be given a seat.

parts.label: (i)

prompt.t: The airline sells 13 tickets. Write down the probability that more passengers turn up than there are seats.

sampleAnswer.t: All 13 must turn up: probability $\left(\dfrac{47}{50}\right)^{13}$.

classification.content: Binomial distribution; expected values; decision making

parts.keyChecks: verified by tools/papers/verify/p09.py: exact binomial P(X>12) for 13 tickets

prompt.t: Show that selling 13 tickets rather than 12 increases the airline's expected income exactly when $C \times \left(\dfrac{47}{50}\right)^{13} < 250$.

text.t: Finds the expected compensation when 13 tickets are sold

sampleAnswer.t: Selling one more ticket brings in $250 more. With 13 tickets at most one passenger is turned away, which happens with probability $\left(\dfrac{47}{50}\right)^{13}$, so the expected compensation is $C \times \left(\dfrac{47}{50}\right)^{13}$ (with 12 tickets it is 0). So the expected income increases exactly when $C \times \left(\dfrac{47}{50}\right)^{13} < 250$.

classification.content: Binomial distribution; expected values; decision making

prompt.t: The airline sells 14 tickets. Show that the expected number of passengers who cannot be given a seat is $\left(\dfrac{47}{50}\right)^{13}\left(14 - 12 \times \dfrac{47}{50}\right)$.

text.t: Finds the probabilities that 13 and 14 passengers turn up
Recognises that 1 or 2 passengers may be turned away

sampleAnswer.t: One passenger is turned away if exactly 13 turn up, with probability $14 \times \left(\dfrac{47}{50}\right)^{13}(1 - \dfrac{47}{50})$, and two are turned away if all 14 turn up, with probability $\left(\dfrac{47}{50}\right)^{14}$. So the expected number is $14 \left(\dfrac{47}{50}\right)^{13}(1 - \dfrac{47}{50}) + 2 \times \left(\dfrac{47}{50}\right)^{14} = \left(\dfrac{47}{50}\right)^{13}\left(14 - 14 \dfrac{47}{50} + 2 \times \dfrac{47}{50}\right) = \left(\dfrac{47}{50}\right)^{13}\left(14 - 12 \times \dfrac{47}{50}\right)$.

classification.content: Binomial distribution; expected values; decision making

parts.label: (iv)

prompt.t: Find the greatest whole number of dollars $C$ for which selling 14 tickets gives a greater expected income than selling 13.

text.t: Obtains the inequality $C\left(E_2 - E_1\right) < 250$ with the expected numbers $E_1$, $E_2$ turned away

sampleAnswer.t: The extra ticket brings $250, and the expected compensation rises by

C\left(\left(\dfrac{47}{50}\right)^{13}(14 - 12 \times \dfrac{47}{50}) - \left(\dfrac{47}{50}\right)^{13}\right) = C \times \left(\dfrac{47}{50}\right)^{13}\left(13 - 12 \times \dfrac{47}{50}\right) \approx 0.7695\,C.
So we need $0.7695\,C < 250$, that is, $C < 324.90$. The greatest whole number of dollars is 324.

classification.content: Binomial distribution; expected values; decision making

parts.keyChecks: verified by tools/papers/verify/p09.py: exact Fractions: expected income for 13 and 14 tickets from the full binomial distributions; largest integer C with income14>income13

prompt.t: A vase is formed by rotating the curve $x = 2y$, for $0 \le y \le 4$, about the $y$-axis (units in decimetres). Water is poured into the empty vase at a constant rate of $6$ dm$^3$ per second. Let $h$ be the depth of the water at time $t$ seconds.
Show that the volume of water when the depth is $h$ is $\dfrac{4 \pi h^{3}}{3}$.

text.t: Writes the volume as an integral with respect to $y$

sampleAnswer.t: $V = \pi\displaystyle\int_0^h x^2\,dy = \pi\int_0^h 4 y^{2}\,dy = \dfrac{4 \pi h^{3}}{3}$.

classification.content: Volumes of solids of revolution; related rates

parts.label: (ii)

prompt.t: Find the rate at which the depth is increasing when $h = 2$.

sampleAnswer.t: $\dfrac{dV}{dh} = 4 \pi h^{2}$ and $\dfrac{dV}{dt} = 6$, so $\dfrac{dh}{dt} = \dfrac{6}{4 \pi h^{2}}$. At $h = 2$ this is $\dfrac{3}{8 \pi}$ dm per second.

classification.content: Volumes of solids of revolution; related rates

parts.keyChecks: verified by tools/papers/verify/p09.py: V(h) by mpmath quadrature, dV/dh by differentiation, dh/dt=6/(dV/dh) at h=2

parts.label: (iii)

prompt.t: Find the time taken to fill the vase to a depth of $2$ dm.

sampleAnswer.t: The volume at depth $2$ is $\dfrac{32 \pi}{3}$, and water enters at $6$ dm$^3$ per second, so the time is $\dfrac{16 \pi}{9}$ seconds.

classification.content: Volumes of solids of revolution; related rates

parts.keyChecks: verified by tools/papers/verify/p09.py: V(2) by quadrature divided by 6 dm^3/s

parts.label: (iv)

prompt.t: Find the depth at the instant when the depth is increasing at $\dfrac{1}{\pi}$ dm per second.

sampleAnswer.t: $\dfrac{dh}{dt} = \dfrac{6}{4 \pi h^{2}} = \dfrac1{\pi}$ gives $h^2 = \dfrac{3}{2}$, so $h = \dfrac{\sqrt{6}}{2}$ dm.

classification.content: Volumes of solids of revolution; related rates

parts.keyChecks: verified by tools/papers/verify/p09.py: root-find of 6/(dV/dh)=1/pi using the quadrature V(h)
